event: Nala hands Dickon's belt to Jory.
He takes it with a bow of the head. "I'll carry it to his mother at Brennock Ford."
"The Wend Maid owes you passage anywhere on the Wend, any time. Free."
Nala takes the towpath back north under the willows; the walk passes quietly.
A little before half past two she reaches Wendlow's gate, mouth dry from the road.
The watch knows her now. She pays her copper and is waved through with a grin.
At Antler Hall she unwraps the two hooked, yellow-white fangs on the counter.
Grete turns one over. "Eighty pounds of head is too much to haul. These will do."
"Box is empty since your last lot," she says, and writes a chit for fifteen gold.
"Paid with the other when the tax rider comes tomorrow." She signs it and slides it over.
She hangs the fangs on a nail beside Voss's head and wipes the Weir Wyrm off the Board.
"That letter went to the magistrate yesterday," she adds, low. "That's all I'll say of it."
"Board's bare till the rider brings fresh slips tomorrow," Grete says, and dips her pen in the ink.
